requirements.statement: For each prerecorded audio-only media that has a text transcript, outside the particular cases, the transcript is relevant.

citations.quote: Pour chaque média temporel pré-enregistré seulement audio, ayant une transcription textuelle, celle-ci est-elle pertinente (hors cas particuliers)
Pour chaque média temporel seulement audio, vérifier que transcription textuelle est pertinente

routes.statement: The transcript gives, in chronological order, everything said in the media and all the descriptive information needed for an equivalent understanding.

citations.quote: La totalité de ce qui y est exprimé oralement
Toutes les informations descriptives nécessaires à une compréhension équivalente de l’action.
Ces informations textuelles doivent être présentées dans l’ordre chronologique de leur apparition dans le média temporel.

exceptions.statement: The media is decorative: it carries no information.

rationale.text: The test asks whether the transcript of each prerecorded audio-only media is relevant. The glossary defines a transcript as giving everything said and all the descriptive information needed, in chronological order. Comparing a text with what a recording says is judgment: it needs someone to listen and read. No axe rule is tagged for this test, and no deterministic check can decide relevance, so there are no links and the entry stays at none. A missing transcript is not a fault here: it makes this test not applicable to the media and belongs to criterion 4.1. The particular cases of criterion 4.1 apply to this criterion by their own text and are listed as exceptions; all of them need judgment or facts the page does not hold (decorative use, publication date). Applicability is judgment: whether a media is prerecorded, audio-only and has a transcript cannot be decided from the markup with certainty. Needs lists media, because the content of the recording is known only once it plays.
